title: ACID Transactions, Isolation Levels & Safe Migrations
summary: Prevent race conditions (double-spending/overbooking) using explicit transactions, row locking (`FOR UPDATE`), and zero-downtime Expand-Contract schema migrations.
learningObjectives: Prevent concurrent double-spend races cleanly using transactional locks and atomic conditional updates
Execute zero-downtime database migrations via the Expand-Contract strategy
prerequisiteConcepts: Understanding of INSERT/UPDATE and basic indexes

sections.heading: 1. Atomic Transactions & Preventing Check-Then-Act Races
sections.content:
Imagine two concurrent HTTP requests checking a student wallet (`balance = 100`) simultaneously: both read `100 >= 80`, then both subtract `80`, corrupting the ledger (`-60`)! This **Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU)** race condition vanishes inside explicit transactions (`BEGIN ... COMMIT`) using atomic updates (`UPDATE wallets SET balance = balance - 80 WHERE id = $1 AND balance >= 80`) or pessimistic row locks (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`).

For concurrent multi-row transfers, always lock account IDs in a sorted canonical order (`LEAST(id1, id2)` first!) so concurrent opposite transfers NEVER trigger circular deadlocks!

codeExamples.code:
Request A (Debit 80) ---> [BEGIN] -> UPDATE WHERE balance >= 80 -> [1 row updated -> COMMIT]
Request B (Debit 80) ---> [Wait on Lock] ----------------------> WHERE balance >= 80 FALSE -> 0 rows -> Safe Rollback!
codeExamples.explanation: Row locks + atomic predicates prevent concurrent requests from double-spending the exact same balance.

keyPoints: Never perform 'read into Node memory -> check in JS -> separate UPDATE' without locking or conditional WHERE guards.
Expand-Contract migrations add new columns cleanly first, backfill safely, update code, then drop legacy columns later without outages.
commonMistakes: Renaming or dropping actively queried columns directly (`ALTER TABLE ... RENAME COLUMN`) while older deployed app containers still query the old name!

sections.heading: 2. Atomic Conditional Wallet Deduction & Audit Insert
sections.content: Check how combining `RETURNING` and conditional `WHERE` inside an explicit `BEGIN ... COMMIT` makes financial state updates mathematically atomic.

codeExamples.explanation: Checking `balance_cents >= 5000` inside the `UPDATE` holds the row lock atomically avoiding stale JS reads.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Atomic balance reduction strictly blocked when funds < 5000, committed alongside immutable audit row

keyPoints: Check `ROLLBACK;` cleanly in `catch` blocks whenever any intermediate statement fails.
commonMistakes: Leaving uncommitted idle transactions (`BEGIN` without `COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`) hanging, holding table locks and blocking `VACUUM` cleanup.

exercises.title: Solve Concurrent Seat Booking Overbooking Race
exercises.objective: Prevent concurrent reservations from exceeding workshop seat capacity.
exercises.description: Two users simultaneously click 'Reserve Seat' on a live workshop with `seats_remaining = 1`. Fix the naive JS read-then-write logic (`if (workshop.seats > 0) update seats = seats - 1`).
instructions: Wrap reservation inside a clean PostgreSQL `BEGIN ... COMMIT` block.
Use an atomic conditional `UPDATE workshops SET seats_remaining = seats_remaining - 1 WHERE id = $1 AND seats_remaining >= 1 RETURNING id`.
Insert the reservation row ONLY if `UPDATE` matched 1 row; otherwise `ROLLBACK`.
hints: Putting `AND seats_remaining >= 1` directly inside the atomic `UPDATE` serializes competing row updates cleanly.
exercises.submissionRequirements: Complete all checklist items, test assumptions, and document verification rationale.
evaluationCriteria: Addresses the root architectural/technical challenge accurately
Follows defensive industry standards and edge-case validation
exercises.solutionExplanation: The first request decrements `1 -> 0` and succeeds; the second blocks briefly on row lock, evaluates `0 >= 1` (false), updates 0 rows, and aborts cleanly with zero overbooking.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why does checking `if (wallet.balance >= amount)` in Node.js memory followed by a separate `UPDATE wallets SET balance = balance - amount` risk negative balances?

options.text: Concurrent requests can both read the old positive balance before either commits (TOCTOU race condition)
Node numbers turn negative on JSON parse
JavaScript floats round numbers down automatically

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Atomic database-level `WHERE balance >= amount` or `SELECT FOR UPDATE` closes race windows cleanly.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What ACID guarantee ensures that if step 2 (audit log insert) fails mid-transaction, step 1 (balance deduction) is completely undone?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Atomicity makes every multi-statement transaction strictly all-or-nothing.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: How does the Expand-Contract migration pattern rename a live column with zero deployment downtime?

options.text: Add new column + dual-write/backfill -> update deployed code reads -> drop old column once old pods terminate
Run RENAME COLUMN immediately during peak hours
Truncate the table before running ALTER TABLE
Restart Postgres ignoring running web queries

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Overlap-tolerant transitions prevent rolling pods from crashing on missing column errors.
